prompt:
## STRUCTURE MUST KEEP
Generate ONE finished game-environment concept image: DOWNTOWN / COOL NIGHT / RAIN-WET ROAD AND NEON / BUILDINGS OF TWO TO FOUR STOREYS / A CAR. One complete standalone quarter-view diorama, one single ORTHOGRAPHIC parallel-projection camera. Reference1 is the scene-specific structural guide. Every same-world-direction straight line stays parallel: base, paving, footings, storey bands, window/door horizontals, setback terrace beams and upper roof edges share the same X/Y directions. Vertical lines share one direction. Do not draw the upper buildings from a lower or more frontal camera than the base. No convergence or distance-based scaling. Curved-corner tangents and pitched surfaces are distinct from level straight structural lines.

Use a sharp-cornered square ground footprint with a consistent downward extrusion and TWO fully visible planar front cutaway faces. Same-depth corresponding corner displacements must have the same direction and screen length. Show the complete base, the tops of all buildings, rear boundary ends and every attached component inside the frame with breathing room. No base curvature, bevel, added corner, warped thickness or bowed pavement. Do not let darkness, wet reflections, vehicles or foreground props hide all long diagnostic base edges and building-footing segments. No connected structures or wires extending out of frame.

The two adjacent rear directions are blocking boundaries except for EXACTLY TWO functional transitions, one rear-left and one rear-right. Boundaries can combine the buildings with substantial retained concrete walls, linked urban utility structures and repaired metal panels. Close undesignated gaps. Clear the central roadway, broad turn, approach and both transition volumes of vehicles, barriers and stock. Both exits are OPEN STREET CONTINUATIONS in this scene, not storefront doors or extra arches. Front soil cuts are not additional exits.

Main building placement and straight structural directions follow common ground axes. Develop the stepped building, deep facade recesses and rounded corner building in reference1 with credible thickness, grounding and supports. Do not rotate buildings arbitrarily or create narrow wedge-shaped gaps. Ground-level curved walls are allowed and must have continuous readable contact with the pavement; do not conceal them inside big rectangular plinths. Keep the square base unchanged. The user's TWO-TO-FOUR-STOREY request governs this scene: a four-storey building and a two-storey building with coherent human-scale floors, not compressed miniature floors. This is a scene-specific height choice. Do not increase the storey count with extra rooftop houses.

## CURRENT SCENE
A compact inhabited downtown road bend at NIGHT, predominantly cool blue-gray and desaturated teal. The asphalt and sidewalk have been wetted by rain. Use legible controlled CYAN and MAGENTA NEON strips/panels, a few restrained warm windows, and localized broad reflections that identify the light sources. Reflections follow the flat paving surface, with small shallow puddles and darker matte breaks, never a glassy raised floor or uniformly mirror-like water. Keep enough cool ambient sky illumination to read walls, footings, road and cut faces. No unrequested fog. The background is a quiet dark urban atmospheric gradient with faint distant silhouettes; all foreground diorama boundaries remain independently framed.

BUILDING A on the rear-left is FOUR STOREYS: two broader lower floors with two narrower upper floors set back asymmetrically. Its large architectural identity comes from unequal wings, deep recessed windows, a sheltered ground entrance and visible terrace depth, not a tall unbroken cube. Use broad patched painted-concrete wall planes and a substantial reused mechanical spine fitted into a vertical service recess. This spine has a few large industrial housings, adapters and rerouted power feeds; repairs are visually functional. Each of the four floors is readable. All floor bands and terrace beams follow the same base axes. Ground doors are ordinary closed entrances and are not map exits.

BUILDING B toward the rear-right is TWO STOREYS and lower/wider in proportion, with a genuinely rounded ground-level corner and a recessed double-height-looking facade rhythm that STILL clearly resolves into two floors. A large reclaimed heat-exchange module is integrated into its roof and exterior service bay, with believable supporting brackets and a maintenance path. Give it a grounded recognizable human entrance. Keep its rounded facade, deep door/window reveals and larger machine housing distinct from A's angular setbacks. Do not turn it into the previous retro appliance workshop or a scrap-yard sorting machine.

Building roofs/setback upper surfaces each have about40–80% purposeful functional composition: A has a connected roof service core, maintenance platform and supported cooling/canopy components on its setback terraces; B has the large integrated heat-exchange cover and access platform, with substantial quiet open roof area. Do not count paint/grime/shadows as coverage and do not fill roofs with arbitrary repeated tiny boxes. Machinery forming a functional roof assembly does not require a duplicate pile of machinery above it. All components rest on visibly coherent supports; no floating rooftop devices.

The road enters at the rear-left gap beside A, travels along a broad clear stretch and bends at a spacious central turn to continue through the rear-right gap beside B. Keep road directions orthogonal in world space; no arbitrary diagonal lane cutting the square. Sidewalks, clear street width and curb transitions distinguish this place from a generic empty courtyard. Simple restrained lane markings may be used, but no letters, numbers or arrows. Both street transitions have visible level continuation and enough unobstructed width and overhead clearance. Ordinary building doors do not add extra functional exits.

Place ONE believable compact passenger car in a small curbside parking area near the front-left portion, aligned with the street, outside the through lane, turn and both exits. Give the car a modest repaired panel or replaced trim consistent with daily use, wet paint and restrained neon reflections. Its roof/windows/wheels must follow the common camera and sit convincingly on the road. Keep it low enough to preserve the view of the center and front cut faces. No people, robots or monsters. Do not import the previous wasteland, scrap piles, daylight or fixed retro-device reference selection.

Salvage Cyberpunk remains the world: old municipal buildings and obsolete advanced equipment are kept working through replacement housings, visibly adapted joints, repaired service lines and reused components. Neon lights do not substitute for these physical repair relationships. The city is occupied and maintained but worn, not a pristine futuristic showroom and not an all-over ruined junk heap. Tell age through a few substantial patched panels and selective wear, while keeping broad surfaces cleanly expressed.

Two front cut faces show large urban foundations, a rainwater collection/drainage service and a repaired electrical trunk tied to this wet downtown street. Use only a few broad, readable ducts/pipes and calm earth/concrete strata. No basement room, door-like hole, repeated tiny pipe grid or copied wasteland cutaway. Preserve visible corresponding corners. This is a fresh city design from the masters; no previous generated image is a reference.

## ART / REFERENCE ROLES
Use Little Devil Inside's architectural/material/light/color expression ONLY, not its story, period setting or characters. Large readable volumes, broad calm base colors, sparse broad directional flat brushwork and nearby-tone patches even on intact areas, separately from selected paint wear. Retain generous quiet surfaces. Use coherent big light/shadow masses and material-appropriate behavior: matte painted walls, metal housings with controlled highlights, dark glazing and genuinely wet asphalt with selective reflections. Flat painted variation must not look like raised impasto, wavy glass, small mosaic marks or fine repetitive dirt. Avoid photoreal miniature micro-detail, dense rivets, all-over rust/gravel/noise, featureless blur, all-plastic materials or extreme faceted low-poly.

Reference1: custom scene geometry and large forms ONLY: square base, one common camera,4/2-storey stepped/curved architecture, two rear street transitions and parked car location. Guide colors, outlines, labels and primitive finish are not final art. Develop deep functional architecture while preserving the common geometry.
Reference2 M01-01: isolated diorama framing and two cut faces only. Do not copy its source perspective, building arrangement, Japanese shop identity, signs or pipe design. Current user independently requests neon; design new neon lighting for this scene rather than transferring M01's theme.
Reference3 M02-01: two rear blocking directions, one functional exit in each and clear central connectivity only; no blue diagram walls, fixed gate coordinates, icons or text.
Reference4 M03-10: primary LDI rendering, large material/color planes and selective detail only. Exclude original shops, people, text, daylight and source camera/layout.
Reference5 M04-02: large recovered industrial mechanical volumes, painted housings and functional joints only, adapted into city service architecture. Exclude the person, exoskeleton silhouette, pose, photoreal texture and source camera. M04-08 retro collage is not an input for this request.

Mandatory orthographic geometry overrides every source camera. No readable lettering, numbers, logos, watermarks, arrows or UI. Neon may be abstract illuminated panels/strips/shapes without invented text. No green CRT. One final scene only, no montage or comparison sheet.
